content.thinking:
I should plan out a whimsical biplane design in one careful write: a chubby fuselage, round engine cowl, oversized propeller and wheels, bright cream/red/teal/yellow colors, with a root joint around [0,1.2,0], roughly 7.5m long and 8m wingspan.

Mapping out joints for propeller, wheels, rudder, elevator, and ailerons off a central "body" joint, and working through fuselage coordinates along the z-axis so the prop and tail skid clear the ground properly. Figuring out a color palette and how to build the fuselage shape using a loft with toon-shaded paints.

Now I'm defining fuselage loft stations at each z-position with their width/height/y-offset, tapering from the cowl back to the tail, and planning out two open cockpit cutouts with dark recessed shapes and cream trim rings along the top of the fuselage.

I want to add character to the cockpits—a goofy pilot with goggles, cap, and a waving scarf in the rear seat, plus a round-eared stuffed bear riding in the front cockpit for charm. For the engine cowl, I'm lathing a profile around the fuselage axis to create the rounded nose shape, building up the outline points that sweep from the center axis outward and back.

Now I'm working out the spinner cone at the propeller hub and the blade shapes—lathing a small yellow spinner tip, then extruding a tapered blade outline with thickness so the propeller has real three-dimensional form rather than flat panels.

I'm mirroring that blade outline to create a second blade pointing the opposite direction, coloring the prop wood-brown with yellow tips based on distance from the hub, and adding small riveted details using merged sphere geometry for the cowl. Now I'm positioning the wings—planning an upper wing around y=2.75 and a lower wing attaching beneath the fuselage near y=1.05.

Working out wing placement and tapered rounded tip outlines...

For the painting I'm designing a surface shader keyed off normal direction and spanwise position, red cel top with cream stripes and yellow tips, cream underside. I'm also planning roundel decals as upward-facing planes on the top wing with a star-in-circle emblem, and sketching out aileron hinge joints on the trailing edge of the upper wing.

Working out aileron geometry...

Still writing outline logic...

Now I'm positioning the lower wing: shorter span, embedded into the fuselage bottom, with a cream underside and red top, no aileron needed there. I'm then placing the interplane struts between upper and lower wings at staggered x positions, working out z-coordinates for front and rear struts so they connect correctly given the wings' chord offsets and stagger.

I'm adding diagonal cross-bracing wires between the lower inner and upper outer wing points, plus cabane struts connecting the fuselage top to the upper wing center section, and settling on the upper wing's vertical position to compute overall aircraft height.

For the tail, I'm shaping the vertical fin and separate hinged rudder using extruded outlines, defining their joint points so the fin and rudder connect smoothly at the hinge line while keeping heights proportionate to the rest of the plane.

Now I'm working out the horizontal stabilizer and elevator planform, extruding shapes relative to a shared origin point near the tail, with the fixed stabilizer forming the front portion and the hinged elevator extending further back, tuning the outline coordinates so both halves align at the hinge.

I'm checking that the rudder, elevator, and stabilizer intersect reasonably near the tail without clipping through the fuselage, and considering adding thin bracing struts from the stabilizer down to the fuselage underside for structural detail.

Now I'm working out the tail skid and tail wheel geometry—placing a rod from the fuselage underside down to near the ground, then adding a small wheel at the base so the tail rests properly above the floor plane.

For the main landing gear, I'm sizing chunky whimsical wheels at radius 0.52 with tires built from torus geometry oriented along the x-axis, positioning the axles so the tires sink just slightly into the floor for a grounded look without clipping too much.

I'm adding cream cylindrical hubs with red caps and a decal plane showing a spoked wheel graphic facing outward, then setting up hinge joints for each wheel so they rotate properly. For the gear structure, I'm running V-shaped struts from the fuselage down to each wheel axle, plus a connecting axle rod between the wheels with cream shock sleeves, keeping it simple without extra fairings.

Now I'm working on the exhaust pipes, sweeping a curved path from the cowl side downward with a chrome-capped tip, and painting the cowl itself with a red cel base and a cream stripe ring near the front rim based on z-position rather than using decals for the vents.

For the radial engine look, I'm adding a yellow cooling torus wrapped around the cowl's front edge instead of individual cylinders. Then I'm setting up the fuselage paint logic: a cream belly using a jagged fur-edge boundary with ink outlining, wrapped in cel shading, plus a custom paint function layering in a teal stripe band across the sides.

For the tail section I'm adding a whimsical touch -- the very tip dips into bright yellow cel shading if it's far enough back. I'm also planning a decal badge on the fuselage side, a cartoon sunburst emblem with the plane's name, applied onto the fuselage loft surface at a specific position.

Actually, I'm worried about text getting mirrored on one side when drawn onto a loft, so I'll skip text entirely and go with a symmetric smiling-sun emblem instead -- safer and still whimsical. I'm also considering thin stitch-line details along the fuselage to suggest fabric seams.

Rather than a full seam texture, I'll add ribbed lines along the wings at regular spacing for a stitched look, then move on to positioning the pilot's head sphere near the rear of the cockpit.

Working out the cockpit opening next: a dark disk cylinder sits on the fuselage's curved top, framed by a flattened torus for a cream rim, with the pilot's torso and head spheres sized and placed inside, topped by a leather cap hemisphere.

Still designing the pilot...

I'm figuring out where to position the two cockpits relative to the wings, plus laying out fuselage stations with center heights and widths to compute the body's curved profile.

Now I'm placing joints for the moving parts—body root, propeller, wheels, rudder, elevators, and ailerons—figuring out their pivot locations and hinge roles.

Then I'm working out the strut and rigging rods, deciding which joints each wooden strut should bind to and keeping the rigging wires thin and dark, before adding finishing touches like cowl rivets, ribs, a pitot tube, and small glass windscreens.

Now I'm placing those windscreens in front of each cockpit, tilting them back slightly and adding a darker frame box behind for depth, plus a cute headrest fairing hump behind the pilot using a scaled, painted sphere. I'm also planning small glowing spheres for the wingtip navigation lights and a landing light on the cowl.

Working out positions for the cowl rivets now—lathing the cowl profile along the fuselage axis to form a lip wider than the body, defining the spinner shape at the prop joint, and computing a ring of small rivet spheres spaced around the cowl's circumference using sine/cosine placement.

I'm adding small cowl vent louvre boxes on the sides, slightly embedded into the curved cowl surface at a few y-offsets. For wing markings, I'm planning roundel decals textured as circles with stars, placed on the top and underside of the upper/lower wings using plane geometry oriented outward.

Now I'm writing the wing paint function: edges get a cream rim tone, the top surface uses a red base with periodic rib lines in darker red, a cream leading-edge band, and yellow wingtips, while the underside uses cream with shadow-shaded ribs via the normal-based cel shading. I'm also sketching aileron coloring, likely teal with a cream edge stripe.

For the fuselage I'm lofting a default circular cross-section with increased sides for smoothness, tapering stations by width and height, adding a rounded tail cap and belly keel detail. I'm defining the exhaust as a swept tube along a curved path with rounded caps and a small dark tip sphere, then sketching an SVG texture for the wheel hub with concentric circles and spokes to be mapped onto an outward-facing plane.

Now I'm working out hub and tire geometry so the hub cylinder fills the torus tire's inner hole correctly, sizing the hub plane and cylinder radius to match, then sketching an SVG sun emblem with radiating triangular rays rotated around a center circle for the fuselage decal.

I'm placing the pilot emblem position on the fuselage side, figuring out coordinates relative to cockpit height and depth, then moving on to paint tail fin and rudder stripe patterns using y-position checks to assign red, cream, and teal bands, and sketching simple capsule arms for the pilot reaching toward a central control stick.

Now I'm detailing the pilot figure itself: a jacket-shaped body, scarf, skin-toned head with a leather flying cap and earflaps, a strap-mounted goggle assembly with tinted lenses and rims, plus small facial features like nose, mustache, and cheeks to give it character. I'm then starting on a small bear figure with a simple spherical head.

Adding bear ears, snout, nose...

I decide the vehicle doesn't need ground chocks or a wing walker, and skip the trailing banner idea, but I add a pitot tube rod on one of the wing struts. Then I sketch out small triangular pennant flags mounted on poles at the top wing tips, working out the pole height and flag outline geometry before placing them.

I color the pennants alternating red and yellow, skip the fuel tank idea on the top wing center, and verify ground clearance — wheels, tail wheel, and propeller all sit safely above zero. Finally I work out the propeller blade geometry and paint logic, giving the wood blades yellow tips and checking the extrusion axes so both blades orient correctly around the spinner hub.

Now I'm sorting out TypeScript typing concerns for the outline points and extrude helper functions, making sure tuples and paint return types satisfy the expected interfaces.

Writing imports and setup...

Now I'm defining the color palette and helper functions for outlines and mirroring, then sketching the wing-building logic with extruded outline shapes and bevels, starting to lay out the coordinate points for the upper wing's outline.

Still mapping aileron and lower wing outline coordinates...

Checking the wing leading edge clearance over the cowl confirms it works. Now I'm defining a wing paint function that colors the rim, top, and ribs differently based on surface normal and position along the span.

Writing wing colors...

I'm sketching out the fuselage paint function next, handling the belly versus upper fuselage color transition at a given height threshold.

Still defining the belly edge function...

Still writing paint logic...

Pilot jacket collar is cream fur, and I'm adding merged rivet spheres to the body geometry for metal detail, placed via the part helper. I'll skip extra wing rivet lines but consider small metal fitting boxes at the interplane strut ends.

For the fuselage decal, I'm placing a sun emblem behind the cockpit on the side of the fuselage using the decal helper with position, direction, and size tuned to the surface width there. Then I'm setting up the tail wheel hinge joint and tire geometry at the rear of the fuselage.

Now I'm adding a skid rod shock sleeve near the tail, a glowing wingtip light sphere, and standard aviation navigation lights -- red on the left wingtip, green on the right -- positioned at the wing extremities.

Still placing components...

Working through rudder paint bands, fin and rudder extrusion geometry, and the hinge joints for stabilizer, elevator, and rudder, making sure their z-ranges line up along the tail without gaps.

Now I'm planning the bracing wires between fin and stabilizer, confirming the fuselage loft ordering runs nose-to-tail, and double-checking cowl versus fuselage radii and cockpit coaming details before writing the actual part-generation code with helper functions, joints for the wheel, and Euler rotations for flat torus pieces.

Setting up wheel hubs, axles, and gear strut fairings...

Cleaning up unused imports like furEdge and shadowOf, keeping zigzag and ink utilities that are actually used, and double-checking paint color constants work correctly for the torso sphere and goggle strap elements.

Now I'm placing the goggle strap torus and moustache spheres relative to the head center, checking that the head position clears the upper wing height, then adding the windscreen and its metal frame boxes at the right rotation and position relative to the fuselage, verifying the vertical clearance works out. I'm finalizing the structure, explicitly tagging static parts to the body bone before composing the final output.
